correctness.rationale: For a vertex-minimal induced flag support with nonzero reduced H_d, deletion and the star-link exact sequence force nonzero H_{d-1} in every link, and no vertex is universal. Induction from d=0 gives 2d+2 vertices; equality forces the complement graph to be a perfect matching. This applies to any nonzero ambient image, and the octahedral opposite pairs are exactly incident input edges from disjoint three-vertex paths. Here six paths partition the graph. An independent exact reproduction using vertex deletion for faces, branching on the least uncovered graph vertex for partitions, and distance-preserving bijections for automorphisms recovered 297 supports, 216 automorphisms and the stated orbit representatives and sizes. Global Hasse acyclicity and a 43-by-3 critical boundary with a +1 minor on rows (2,3,15) were checked. Subtracting signed paired coface boundaries in topological order kills the matched lower coordinates over Z. The surviving matched-upper coordinates are determined for cycles because their down-boundary block is unit triangular. Every one of the 5,319 original degree-six boundaries has critical image in the span of the three critical boundary columns, so the resulting map on H_5 into Z^40 is injective. The stated 40 orbit-0 cycles have determinant -1, making it onto. All 297 signed cycles had zero boundary and gcd-one quotient coordinates. Exact Smith forms gave ranks (40,25,35,31,5) and index one for all five orbits.
residual_risks: The reproduction relies on finite enumerations and exact signed integer algebra, with the stated graph labeling and cycle orientation; it is not proof-assistant verification.

The isolated phrase 'a different 43-by-three Morse certificate' in the prior-work paragraph is inaccurate: the earlier record uses the same toggle order and the same signed degree-five matrix. The current augmented poset adds the pairing of the empty simplex with the previous critical vertex. This attribution detail does not affect the Finding or the integral certificate.

value.rationale: The question is how homology of a standard symmetric graph can be generated from smallest induced subcomplexes, not what its known Betti number is. The result classifies every minimal inclusion class and distinguishes equal-size symmetry orbits with different ranks (40 versus 35). The explicit basis in one orbit provides usable integral generators with minimal supports. These are measurable distinctions not recoverable from the homotopy type alone.
residual_risks: A classification for this graph and degree, not evidence of a cubic-graph family theorem.
